name: figure-1 benchmark v01
status: frozen before any held-out outcome of scenarios S1 (D2c), S2 (block D2) or S3 (striker D3) exists
common_question: After the same initial footage and the same single calibration interaction, which method best predicts a new interaction?

methods.ours: posterior over material parameters with FEM forward model; observations = markers tracked in the SAME RGB frames the baselines receive, triangulated from two fitting cameras (no depth)
methods.GIC: official b523851 on raw RGB, cameras 1-10; native fit on initial footage, native refit on calibration footage; labelled force adapter; striker via labelled contact adapter (forecast only)
methods.PAC-NeRF: official b613048 on raw RGB, cameras 1-10; same protocol as GIC; same labelled adapters
methods.M-PhyGs: blocked: image-fitting stage requires tiny-cuda-nn; not run (reported, not scored)

S1_stem_push.held_out: D2c: 20 N at 0.75 L along (0,-0.8,-0.6) = 16 N down + 12 N toward -z (new direction)
S1_stem_push.score: 3D station-displacement RMS (4 material stations) over all frames, mm

S2_block_press.worlds: block 0.24x0.10x0.12 m, bottom glued, E_soft 6e4 Pa, nu 0.4, rho 1000 (known to all), hidden 8x stiffer region |x-xc|<0.04, y>0.555, xc = -0.06 / 0 / +0.06
S2_block_press.initial: D0 30 N press, centre of top face
S2_block_press.score: 3D displacement RMS of 27 top-surface probe points over all frames, mm

S3_stem_striker.held_out: D3: gravity release + rigid sphere r=0.03 m, m=0.3 kg, centre (0.17,0.60,0.0755), velocity (0,0,-1) m/s; free rebound; contact law b = 1e11*(r-|x-c|)*n N/m^3 for every method
S3_stem_striker.score: striker impulse error |m dv_pred - m dv_true| in N s (primary), striker rebound velocity, stem station RMS mm

rendering: camera 0 (never used for fitting) foreground PSNR, reported beside physics; appearance per method's own native renderer
rule: all predictions for a scenario sealed (sha256) before its held-out truth is generated; failures retained
known_limits: S1 and S3 share the stem object and its fits (different held-out interactions). Truth is a numerical FEM reference. Ours uses an FEM forward model of the same family as the reference solver (coarser mesh, linear elasticity).
